questions.q: What is the general recipe for a confidence interval for a mean?
options: Sample mean plus or minus the sample standard deviation
Sample mean plus or minus a critical value times the standard error
The minimum and maximum of the sample
The middle 95% of the individual observations
questions.explain: The interval is the estimate plus or minus a critical value (from t or the normal) multiplied by the standard error.

questions.q: Which is the correct interpretation of a 95% confidence interval of 37.87 to 41.37?
options: There is a 95% probability that the true mean lies in this specific interval
95% of individual deliveries fall between 37.87 and 41.37
If we repeated the sampling and interval procedure many times, about 95% of the intervals would contain the true mean
The sample mean has a 95% chance of being correct
questions.explain: The 95% describes the long-run success rate of the procedure. The true mean is a fixed value; a particular interval either contains it or not.

questions.q: You want a 99% interval instead of 95% from the same sample. What happens to the interval?
options: It becomes narrower
It becomes wider
It stays the same
It shifts but keeps the same width
questions.explain: Greater confidence requires a larger critical value, so the interval widens. In the lesson the width went from 3.49 to 4.68.

questions.q: Roughly how does the width of a 95% CI for a mean change when you quadruple the sample size?
options: It stays the same
It drops to a quarter
It doubles
It drops to about half
questions.explain: Width is proportional to the standard error, which shrinks with the square root of n. Four times the data means about half the width.

questions.q: In the simulation with a strongly skewed population and n = 15, nominal 95% t intervals captured the true mean only about 86% of the time. What does this teach?
options: The confidence level is always exactly the stated value
Skewed data never needs a confidence interval
The t interval can under-cover with small, skewed samples, so larger samples or the bootstrap may be needed
The true mean changes when data is skewed
questions.explain: The t interval's assumptions can fail for small skewed samples, so real coverage can fall below the nominal level.
